text:
oncall-bot: [PAGE] High latency & queueing on Dedicated pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42. 95th token latency > 3s for last 5m, queued requests rising. Affects customers on pool: AcmeAnalytics, FinFlow (high qps customers). Please ack.

alex: acked. jumping in. any recent deploys?

maria: no deploys in last hour. I see a spike in request rate from client_id=acme-analytics-org around 12:03UTC. CPU on g4 instances at 92%. KV cache miss rate up 3x.

sam: is autoscaling not catching up? what's current desired replicas?

maria: desired=8, running=8, pending scaling blocked by reserved capacity config. Looks like burst capacity is currently disabled after yesterday's experiment.

alex: ok, immediate mitigations: 1) enable burst capacity +40% for 20m 2) apply soft QPS cap to noisy tenants 3) route non-critical routes to cheaper model variant to offload tokens. I'll do 1 & 2.

alex: running: 
```
redwoodctl pools toggle-burst --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 --enable --percent 40 --duration 20m
```

ops-bot: Command received: toggle-burst on eu-west-1-dedicated-42
ops-bot: Validating...
ops-bot: Burst capacity enabled: +40% for 20m (expires in 19m 58s)

maria: confirming metrics now. CPU dropping to 78%, queue length decreasing. 95p latency falling from 3.2s -> 1.6s within 60s.

alex: applying qps throttles to top noisy keys:
```
redwoodctl quotas set --org acme-analytics --qps 10 --scope api
redwoodctl quotas set --org finflow --qps 15 --scope api
```

ops-bot: quotas updated for acme-analytics (10 qps), finflow (15 qps)

sre-pager: noting customer impact: AcmeAnalytics reports degraded scores on embeddings extraction; some jobs retried. Left a message to their SRE: "We observed high-latency, applied throttling and temporary burst to restore SLOs. Will follow up with post-incident writeup." :wave:

jess: do we need to fallback to smaller model to reduce token load for non-critical endpoints? We could route /v1/embeddings to embed-smaller for non-verified keys.

maria: good idea. I can add a temporary route rule. Running:
```
redwoodctl routing add-rule --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 --match "route:/v1/embeddings and key not in verified_keys" --target embed-small --duration 30m
```

ops-bot: Routing rule added. Affected traffic should decrease ~22%.

alex: 95p latency now ~1.1s, error rate normalizing. Queue length back to baseline in last 3m.

sam: thanks. I'm taking over the on-call at 13:00UTC — can you leave a short handoff note with what actions were taken and any follow-ups?

alex: handoff note:
- root cause: sudden qps spike from AcmeAnalytics + burst disabled blocked autoscale
- mitigations executed: enabled burst +40% for 20m, applied QPS caps for noisy orgs, added routing rule to use embed-small for non-verified keys
- current status: stable; latency SLO restored, queue normal
- follow-ups: investigate why burst toggles were disabled yesterday (PR #3421), add alert for burst-disabled+high-queue, run retrospective with PL

alex: paging off for me, Sam owns from here. @sam take it.

sam: ack. I will 1) keep burst enabled until 13:20UTC unless metrics degrade, 2) open incident ticket and assign postmortem, 3) coordinate customer comms. Creating ticket now.

sam: created INC-2026 in our tracker: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026. Assigning to eng-runtime (maria) and infra (kamal).

kamal: noted. I'll look at autoscale policy logs and the reserved capacity change that blocked scaling. Might be a mismatch in pool tags with reserved_contract=TRUE.

maria: adding perf graphs to the ticket and saving the routing and quota commands to incident notes.

sre-pager: also add customer incident messages sent: AcmeAnalytics notified, FinFlow contacted. We'll follow up with SLA impact assessment.

sam: leaving on-call Handoff summary for next shift:
- active mitigations (do not revert until follow-ups done): burst +40% (expires 13:20UTC), QPS caps on AcmeAnalytics/FinFlow, routing rule for embed-small
- contacts: alex (shift end), maria (metrics), kamal (scaling infra), jess (routing)

sam: closing the page for now. please escalate in this thread if anything regresses. :thumbsup: 

oncall-bot: Note: burst toggle will auto-expire at 13:20UTC. Manual disable available via `redwoodctl pools toggle-burst --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-42 --disable`.

sam: logged follow-up tasks in INC-2026: investigate burst-disabled regression, add alert for queued_requests>50 & burst_disabled, review reserved capacity policy, postmortem owner: maria.

alex: thanks team. Leaving a quick blameless note: noisy client backpressure and an accidental config change. We'll schedule a retro and make burst toggles safer.

kamal: I'll also add a small automation to prevent burst toggles from being left disabled for >2h without an owner.

jess: will coordinate communications with support for impacted customers.

sre-pager: thread archived after sam closes the incident. Good recovery. :white_check_mark:
